newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to buy 300 trucks from Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to buy 300 trucks from Turkey.

text.p: Iraq will buy 300 trucks from Turkey to transport food and medicine to Baghdad in accordance with an "oil-for-food" deal signed by Iraq and the U.N. in May, the official newspaper al-Thawra reported on Friday.

The paper, quoting the head of Iraq's State Company for Land Transport who just ended a four-day visit to Ankara, said both countries had agreed on a new plan to transport some of Iraq's imports of food and medicine allowed by the agreement.
"We have agreed with the Turkish side to buy 300 brand new trucks from Turkey," the company's director-general Sami al- Mashhadani told the paper.

"We have also agreed on a new formula to transport food, medicine and other humanitarian needs which arrive in Turkish ports for Iraq's favour under the memorandum of understanding signed between Iraq and the United Nations," he said.
The paper, however, did not say how Iraq was going to pay to Turkey for the trucks.

The agreement, blocked over security concerns in northern Iraq, allows Baghdad to sell oil worth $2 billion every six months to buy relief needs for Iraqi population, suffering from stringent U.N. trade sanctions for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
